key_insight: Model-free reinforcement learning can learn effective pulse-level quantum control policies for indirect manipulation of solid-state qubits, even in a noisy spin-bath environment.
engineering_relevance: This suggests RL could become a practical black-box control tool for tuning quantum devices when accurate system models are unavailable or too costly to use.
method: Simulate NV nuclear-spin control in a spin-bath using generalized cluster correlation expansion.
Train model-free RL agents with minimally observable environments and noisy, sparse rewards.
Benchmark RL performance against other state-of-the-art black-box optimization methods for state preparation and gate design.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation-based evaluation across state preparation and qubit-gate tasks, with performance compared against competing black-box optimizers under sparse, noisy feedback.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based, so real hardware performance may drop if noise, partial observability, or reward sparsity differ from the modeled environment.
paper_title: Quantum control of solid state qubits via Reinforcement Learning
